newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower, depressed by Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower, depressed by Ericsson.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower on Monday, weighed down by market heavyweight Ericsson that fell in a bout of profit-taking and with losses in Europe and New York.
The Stockholm general index fell 0.38 percent to 2,985.90 in average turnover of 4.3 billion crowns.
Brokers said the market could continue downwards on Tuesday, slipping back from record highs last week.
"The market feels a little heavy now with the developments in Europe and the U.S. as well as higher debt yields so the market could fall a bit further," one broker said.
Brokers said the focus was now on the Federal Reserve's policy meeting that starts on Tuesday.
Telecoms major Ericsson fell 8.5 to 304.5 crowns. Brokers attributed the slump to profit-taking after steady gains last week. Swedish business newspaper Finanstidningen says share is overpriced.
Car safety equipment Autoliv held its ground during the day, rising 2.5 to 297.5 crowns.
Swedish business daily Dagens Industri said polls show the share is one of the most attractive on Stockholm Stock Exchange.
